<reason>A won by making the scarce-resource tradeoff the live decision rule and showing B never justified why comparative closeness should outrank already-usable coverage, hours, and fares for wheelchair riders themselves. B’s equal-access framing was punchier and the 6-vs-25 contrast landed, but “Neither / share delay and coverage” did not dissolve A’s hard case, and B kept answering a non-accessible evening bus A was not defending. A’s alternative of direct accessibility, coverage, and maximum-wait duties therefore remained the cleaner reason to reject the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2/closing: converting B’s “share delay and coverage” answer into a concession that closer waits still consume real, already-accessible journeys, and catching B’s misread of the evening-route hypo.</best_rebuttal>
